content: The Sparkling Enope Squid, scientifically known as Watasenia scintillans and commonly referred to as the Firefly Squid, belongs to the class Cephalopoda, subclass Coleoidea, and order Teuthida. It is the only species within the genus Watasenia. This squid inhabits the Western Pacific Ocean, typically at depths ranging from 600 to 1200 feet. It exhibits bioluminescent properties, with specialized light-producing organs called photophores located on each of its tentacles. These photophores emit light, which the squid uses to attract small fish, its primary prey. Remarkably, the Sparkling Enope Squid is the only known cephalopod species to possess evidence of color vision. While most cephalopods have a single visual pigment, this species has three visual pigments and a double-layered retina. These unique adaptations likely allow the squid to differentiate between ambient light in its environment and the bioluminescence it encounters or produces. At full maturity, the Sparkling Enope Squid reaches a length of approximately 3 inches. Its lifespan is notably short, lasting only about one year. During the mating season, which occurs from March to June, the squid can illuminate its entire body. This bioluminescent display is thought to play a role in attracting potential mates.
